Subject: Re: MAP for deployment lane decision (technical tradeoffs)

Emma / Olga —

Adding the technical lens. Short version:

- Dedicated (EU-only GPU pool)
  - Pros: strict data isolation, predictable throughput, easier SLA guarantees and on-prem style controls.
  - Cons: commit/lead time for capacity (2–6 weeks to provision at scale), higher baseline cost.

- Hosted (EU-region, shared infra with tenancy and optional KMS)
  - Pros: fastest to pilot, lower upfront cost, immediate access to latest model variants.
  - Cons: additional controls required for strict auditability; we can enable customer-managed KMS and audit log export to your S3.

- Private (customer VPC / on-prem)
  - Pros: maximum control and compliance, aligns with air-gapped/regulatory scenarios.
  - Cons: longer integration, heavier ops, longer lead time for model updates.

Recommendation for pilot: start Hosted (EU) with KMS + audit-log export and baseline SLOs, run an evaluation set (50k tokens/day simulated) for 2 weeks. If acceptance criteria (latency p95 < 350ms, error rate < 0.5%, and cost per 1k tokens within agreed range) are met, plan a transition window to Dedicated for data residency/long-term SLA.

I've attached a short SLA/latency matrix and proposed acceptance criteria.

Attachment: latency-sla-matrix.xlsx

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
